privacy_description: What stays in your browser, when tools connect online, and what the site can see.
privacy_local_title: Your work usually stays in your browser
privacy_local_text: Many tools edit or convert files on your device without uploading them. Some optional features use the internet. Check what each tool says before approving an online action.
privacy_service_title: Basic information needed to load the site
privacy_service_text: Our hosting provider may receive your IP address, browser details, requested page, and access time. That's normal web traffic, not an upload of the documents you're editing.
privacy_analytics_text: The trick-it interface does not require analytics tracking. Hosting providers and external services you choose to use may process network information under their own policies. We'll update this policy before adding analytics collection to the toolbox.
privacy_links_text: Links to source repositories and outside services take you away from trick-it. Please check their own privacy policies before sharing information.
terms_description: Clear, plain-language terms for using trick-it and its browser tools.
terms_use_text: Use trick-it for work, learning, or personal projects. Follow applicable laws, respect others, and double-check results before relying on them. Even a handy converter can make a mistake.
terms_files_title: You're in charge of your files
terms_files_text: Many tools process your input right in the browser. Some features need an approved download or an outside service; check what a tool tells you before you use it. Only work with content you have permission to process.
terms_availability_text: We may fix, update, pause, or remove a tool. Keep your own copy of important work, because a tool might not always be available, even offline.
terms_liability_title: Check before you depend on it
terms_liability_text: Tools are provided as-is and as available. We can't promise that every result is correct or that everything will work all the time. To the extent allowed by law, trick-it isn't responsible for losses from using or being unable to use a tool. Your rights under applicable law still apply.
terms_third_title: Some tools use other people's code
terms_third_text: Tools may live in separate repositories or rely on open-source libraries. Their licenses and notices still apply. Outside services linked from a tool may have their own terms and policies.
policy_description: How trick-it checks, isolates, and manages tools, explained in everyday language.
policy_register_title: We check tools before listing them
policy_register_text: A tool must come from an approved source and include the files our platform expects. Before publishing it, our build checks its source and verifies the downloaded bundle. That helps catch unwanted changes, but it can't guarantee a tool has no bugs.
policy_route_title: Every tool gets its own space
policy_route_text: Each tool opens on a trick-it page inside an isolated browser frame. We keep repository credentials out of the files sent to you. Even if a tool's source repository is private, code delivered to your browser can be inspected.
policy_behavior_text: A tool's isolated frame can't freely contact the internet. It can ask trick-it to handle approved downloads or supported actions, with checks and permission prompts where needed. Some online features send a URL or other information you choose to an external service. Revoking access stops new requests, but can't undo one already completed or cancel browser permissions you granted separately.
policy_remove_title: When a tool leaves the toolbox
policy_remove_text: We may disable or remove a tool if it becomes unsafe, misleading, unavailable, or no longer meets our publishing requirements. We may update these checks as the platform improves.

terms_intro: Just a few ground rules for using the toolbox. No legal maze.
terms_summary: Use the tools responsibly, check important results, and pay attention when a feature needs online access.
terms_illustration_alt: Clay-style illustration of a document with checkmarks and a reassuring blue shield.
policy_intro: Here's how tools earn a place in the toolbox, what they can access, and what we do if something goes wrong.
policy_summary: We check each tool's source before publishing, run tools in separate browser workspaces, and control supported requests to outside services.
policy_limits_text: Isolation helps, but it doesn't prevent every bug or a tool using too much memory or processing power. Read permission prompts, and don't paste passwords, access tokens, or other sensitive data into tools you don't trust.
policy_illustration_alt: Clay-style illustration of an orange toolbox with a wrench, protective shield, and star.
privacy_intro: Your files are yours. Here's what happens to your data when you use the toolbox.
privacy_summary: Most tools work right in your browser. Some features contact other services when needed. The site still receives basic connection data.
privacy_online_title: When a tool connects to another service
privacy_online_text: A tool can request approved public assets or libraries. Their hosts can see ordinary network details, such as your IP address, but trick-it does not attach your tool input or credentials. SEO Checker sends a public URL you approve to Google PageSpeed Insights to inspect that page. The trick-it host does not store the audit response.
privacy_protection_title: Some online features check for abuse
privacy_protection_text: Protected features may use Cloudflare Turnstile to check browser and network signals. Our host verifies the token. Tools that work entirely offline don't need that check.
privacy_storage_title: What stays in your browser after you leave
privacy_storage_text: Your browser can cache tools, offline files, and preferences. You can remove these through your browser's site-data settings. Clearing them may also remove offline access and saved preferences.
privacy_illustration_alt: Clay-style privacy document with a yellow lock, a blue check-mark shield, and leaves.
